notes.title: Devlog #3: Designing a World That Feels Alive
notes.content: [p]For this week’s devlog, we’re catching up with Carl, the Art Director for [i]100 Lives[/i]. Carl’s been with the project from the early days, helping shape the visual identity of Kingstown from the look of individual characters to the overall feel of the world.[/p][p]In this update, Carl shares a glimpse into how the team is building scenes that feel unique and immersive, the challenges of animating expressive characters, and how even the smallest visual details can tell a story.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What did you work on last week, and what’s next?[/b] [/p][p]Last week, I worked on a mix of screens, including the main menu, the "end of a life" scene, and some early ideas for the character builder background and UI. I also added a few new NPCs - each one bringing something different to Kingstown and helping the world feel more alive and diverse. [/p][p][/p][p][b]What’s a new feature, mechanic, or piece of content you're excited about?[/b] [/p][p]One of the things I’m most excited about is how the events will look in the final version of the game. We’ve got a lot of ideas to make each one feel unique and immersive. With varied characters, animation tools, camera direction, and carefully chosen music and ambience, the aim is for no two scenes to feel the same. I think exploring that side of the game will be something players really enjoy. [/p][p][/p][p][b]What’s been the most interesting design or technical challenge recently?[/b] [/p][p]Right now, a tricky part is improving the character animations, especially for posing and speech - to make them feel smoother and more natural. It’s a challenge, but one that’ll be worth it. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Is there anything players might miss if they don’t look closely?[/b] [/p][p]I’d pay close attention to the details of each character, both visually and in how their personalities come through narratively. These little touches should give players a sense of who they are and maybe who they might become. [/p][p][/p][p][b]How is your work helping bring the “100 Lives” concept to life?[/b][/p][p]I’m involved in most of the visual parts of the game, whether it’s creating characters, backgrounds, UI, or helping shape the direction of things like the map, animation concepts, or other design elements.[/p][p][/p][p]As 100 Lives continues to grow, the art team is focused on making each moment feel distinct, memorable, and full of personality. We’ll be back soon with more updates from the rest of the team. In the meantime, don’t forget to wishlist the game on Steam, and keep an eye out! Sometimes the smallest visual details reveal the biggest surprises.[/p][p]See you next time![/p]

notes.title: Devlog #2: Building the Backbone of 100 Lives
notes.content:
[p]Welcome back to the second installment of our devlog series! This time, we spoke with Jose, one of the developers working behind the scenes on 100 Lives. He’s responsible for the GameBook engine, the system that powers the branching stories, evolving choices, and unpredictable outcomes at the heart of the game.[/p][p]Jose’s work focuses on building the tools that support our narrative design, from localization systems to the engine that makes Kingstown’s many storylines come to life. In this devlog, he shares what he’s been working on, what challenges the team has faced, and what players might discover if they look a little closer.
[/p][p][b]What did you work on last week, and what's next?[/b][/p][p]Last week, I focused on updating the game engine that powers GameBook, specifically optimizing the narrative creation processes and enhancing our localization tools for multi-language support. This involved streamlining workflows for our creative team and improving the efficiency of our translation pipeline to ensure consistent quality across different languages.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What's a new feature, mechanic, or piece of content you're excited about?[/b][/p][p]I'm fascinated by how a character's past life can affect subsequent playthroughs—not just cosmetically, but in meaningful ways that impact the environment and the people around you. It's a mechanic that truly embodies the "part roguelike, part sandbox, part 'how did I get here?'" ethos. I'm particularly excited to see how this evolution unfolds after 100 lives and what unexpected combinations emerge. I'm also a huge fan of the game's soundtrack and the cartoonish art style—they really bring Kingstown's chaotic charm to life.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What's been the most interesting design or technical challenge recently?[/b][/p][p]The most interesting challenge has been seeing how the dev team improves the camera movement across the different devices where the game will be available. Each platform—whether mobile, PC, or console—has unique input methods and screen constraints, so creating a camera system that feels intuitive and responsive across all of them while maintaining the same gameplay experience has required significant technical iteration and testing.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Is there anything players might miss if they don't look closely?[/b][/p][p]Always check the corner maps! You'll consistently find interesting events that can evolve your character in unexpected ways. And yes, there will definitely be easter eggs hidden throughout Kingstown for those who pay attention to the details.[/p][p][/p][p][b]How is your work helping bring the "100 Lives" concept to life?[/b][/p][p]My work centers on the narrative foundation and multi-language support that makes the "100 Lives" concept accessible to players worldwide. I provide the creative team with the best possible tools for content creation, ensuring they can craft interconnected stories that work seamlessly across different languages and cultures. By optimizing these core systems, I'm helping ensure that every player, regardless of their language, can experience the full depth and complexity of their 100 journeys through Kingstown.[/p][p][/p][p]We’ll be back soon with more updates from the team. In the meantime, don’t forget to wishlist [i]100 Lives[/i] on Steam and follow us for more behind-the-scenes content. There’s a lot more to discover, and we can’t wait to share it with you.[/p][p]See you in Kingstown.
[/p]

notes.title: Devlog #1: Breathing Life Into 100 Lives (Literally)
notes.content: [p]Welcome to our very first devlog![/p][p][/p][p]We’re starting things off with a behind-the-scenes look at one of the coolest and most foundational features of [b]100 Lives[/b]: the character customization system. To walk us through it, we sat down with Kimberly, our resident Live2D magician and the person making sure your characters don’t just look good, but [i]move[/i] like they mean it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45699384/f9942765d406d16f31fcdd0e7554f1960ff4f3a4.png"][/img][/p][p]From complex rigging setups to secret Easter eggs, here’s what Kimberly’s been up to:[/p][p][/p][p][b]Q: What did you work on last week, and what’s next?[/b][/p][p]Kimberly:[/p][p]Last week I focused on setting up and rigging our character builder in our very own character tool. This will let players fully customize their own characters later in the game. I also updated and rigged Emily, one of our characters, so we have a lively face for our social media. I’ll also keep refining the character builder and start working on some unique NPCs![/p][p][/p][p][b]Q: What’s a new feature, mechanic, or piece of content you're excited about?[/b][/p][p]Kimberly:[/p][p]I’m excited about the depth of the customization system. Players will be able to create characters that evolve across multiple life stages, and I’m not just saying that because that's the main thing I'm working on 👀.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Q: What’s been the most interesting design or technical challenge recently?[/b][/p][p]Kimberly:[/p][p]Keeping track of all the assets, like clothing, facial features and hairstyles, across different life stages has been a real challenge. It’s like a huge puzzle to make sure everything stays consistent and works seamlessly as characters grow and change and get more options for customization.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Q: Is there anything players might miss if they don’t look closely?[/b][/p][p]Kimberly:[/p][p]Can’t say too much yet, but I’ve been thinking about sneaking in some fun references from other games and media. Whether they actually make it into *100 Lives*? We’ll see! 👀[/p][p][/p][p][b]Q: How is your work helping bring the “100 Lives” concept to life?[/b][/p][p]Kimberly:[/p][p]As a Live2D artist, my job is to breathe life into our characters. I take the illustrations from our artist and make them move, and feel a little bit more alive. I think having the characters animated and customizable really makes a huge difference compared to just static ones. ✨[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45699384/e1766f1127e2bdf860392354fd865c3a81607eb6.png"][/img][/p][p]Thank you for joining us for this week’s devlog, and thank you Kimberly for answering our questions![/p][p]We’ll be back soon with more peeks behind the curtain (and possibly a few cursed bug stories). Until then, make sure to wishlist 100 Lives on Steam and keep an eye out for Emily on our social media![/p][p]Let us know if you have any other questions in the comments! 👇[/p]

notes.title: Hello future Kingstown residents!
notes.content: [p]Hey there, future Kingstown Residents! [/p][p]Does the idea of jumping into a world where you could quite literally [b]be anything[/b] or [b]anyone[/b] you want sound awesome to you? [/p][p]How about a world where starting a new life means taking all the best (potentially magical or wacky) parts of your old one to add to what’s new? Okay, how about committing tax evasion in one life to ending up rock-battling Satan in another? (With still plenty of tax evasion on the side…gotta’ pay for those rad guitars somehow).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45699384/85067a0868bbe5d666dbab3fd04280e3187c2410.png"][/img][/p][p]In 100 Lives, you can do all of this and more (Trust us, a -LOT- more). [b]Every hour is a brand-new lifetime[/b], and every choice you make can come back to haunt you. [/p][p][b]Start each life with a fresh look [/b]or carry traits from lives you’ve lived before. Choose your style, shape your personality, and discover who you want to be this time. With rich customization tools, you can reinvent yourself as often (or as weirdly) as you’d like. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45699384/c1ad1a8f5ab27c7c4474bcddd76e09585698c30d.png"][/img][/p][p]But it’s not just about you. [b]The world around you evolves too[/b]. City limits grow, regions unlock, and sometimes an alien invasion turns a quiet valley into a desolate wasteland. [/p][p]Gangs shift power. Ghosts gain hobbies (Who says you can’t be spooky whilst baking some incorporeal cupcakes?). [/p][p]Keep in mind though, the people you meet, friends, enemies, all those chaotic situationships? They might remember you in the next life… even if you don’t remember them. Better stay on your toes![/p][p]Get ready to [b]make decisions that will span multiple lifetimes[/b] and influence everything around you. Every time you complete a life, regardless of what mischief you might have gotten up to, you will unlock a powerful heirloom that can impact your future lives or be used to make unique choices that you wouldn't normally get to make. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45699384/a26f14661e35676749eff0d37e810ebcec8975ce.png"][/img][/p][p]Unlock as many as you can to really make things weird! You’ve heard about [b]Roguelikes [/b]and [b]Roguelites[/b], now it’s time to full-send your best [b]Roguelife [/b]experience! [/p][p]We’re super excited to get 100 Lives into your hands so that you can join us in the journey we’re setting out on to make the best life-sim imaginable. [/p][p]We’re gearing up to create a living, breathing world with you at its heart! [/p][p]So if you’re excited to get into Kingstown, [b][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3864430/100_Lives"]head on over to our Steam page to wishlist[/url][/b] the game and get ready to live your best 100 Lives (Or more, we’re not going to stop you).[/p][p][/p][p]And make sure to follow our [b]resident influencer Emily[/b] on social media! See all the weird stuff happening around Kingstown while we get everything ready behind the scenes:[/p][p] [b]- [url="https://www.tiktok.com/@100lives_official"]TikTok[/url] [/b][/p][p][b]- [url="https://discord.gg/afDnPx57M8"]Discord[/url] [/b][/p][p][b]- [url="https://www.youtube.com/@100LivesOfficial"]YouTube [/url][/b][/p][p][b]- [url="https://www.instagram.com/100livesofficial/"]Instagram[/url][/b][/p]
